'''Gail G. Hanson''', born 22 February 1947 in Dayton, Ohio<ref>{{cite book|title=American Men and Women of science|date=2004|publisher=Thomson Gale}})</ref> is an American experimental particle physicist.

==Career==
Hanson received her PhD from [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] in 1973.<ref name="UCRProfile">{{cite web |title=UCR Profiles - Search & Browse |url=https://profiles.ucr.edu/app/home/profile/gailg |website=profiles.ucr.edu |access-date=29 April 2020}}</ref> She spent sixteen years at [[SLAC National Accelerator Laboratory]], first as a research assistant and then as a permanent staff member.<ref name="Panofsky" /> Whilst there, Hanson participated in the discovery of the J/psi meson and tau lepton. Her work led to the first evidence for quark jet production in electron-positron annihilation,<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Hanson|first1=G.|last2=Abrams|first2=G. S.|last3=Boyarski|first3=A.|last4=Breidenbach|first4=Martin|author-link4=Martin Breidenbach|last5=Bulos|first5=F.|last6=Chinowsky|first6=William|last7=Feldman|first7=G. J.|last8=Friedberg|first8=C. L.|last20=Morehouse|first20=Charles C.|first14=Rudolf R.|url-access=subscription}}</ref> for which she was awarded the 1996 [[Panofsky Prize]] with Roy Schwitters.<ref name="Panofsky">{{cite web |title=2018 Stanley Corrsin Award Recipient |url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/prizes/prizerecipient.cfm?first_nm=Gail&last_nm=Hanson&year=1996 |website=www.aps.org |access-date=29 April 2020 |language=en}}</ref>

In 2002 she was appointed Distinguished Professor of Physics at the [[University of California, Riverside]].<ref name="UCRProfile" />

==Awards and honors==
*Fellow of the [[American Physical Society]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=H&year=2000&unit_id=&institution=|title=APS physics Archive (1990-present)|access-date=13 May 2014}}</ref>
*Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://membercentral.aaas.org/fellows?page=2&LastName=H&Section=All&Country=All&State=All&name=&company=|title=AAAS physics archive|access-date=13 May 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140514041408/http://membercentral.aaas.org/fellows?page=2&LastName=H&Section=All&Country=All&State=All&name=&company=|archive-date=14 May 2014|url-status=dead}}</ref>
*John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation Fellow<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/gail-g-hanson/|title=Gail Hanson|website=John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Fellows}}</ref>
*Winner of the W.K.H. [[Panofsky Prize]] in Experimental Particle Physics from the [[American Physical Society]] (1996)<ref name="Panofsky" />
